plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flower clusters (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. Native to Mexico, it grows outdoors as a large shrub in warm climates and is widely grown as a potted holiday plant elsewhere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, outdoors in subtropical regions such as Florida, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: Poinsettias need long nights of about 12 hours or more for several weeks to develop their colorful bracts, which is why they color up naturally around the winter solstice. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used its sap to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and brightens winter gardens when little else is in bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (November to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea. Over 30,000 cultivars have been named, and in Japan the flower symbolizes the winter season.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with tall, sturdy stalks topped by large trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere and tropical regions it blooms in the warm season, while forced bulbs bloom indoors in the Northern Hemisphere winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); forced indoors in northern winter
plants.location: Native to tropical Americas and the Caribbean; grown in gardens in South Africa, Australia, and South America, and as indoor potted plants in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can bloom again year after year for decades with proper care, and the flower stalk can grow several centimeters in a single day.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and rounded umbels of tubular flowers on tall stems. It thrives in the sunny summer weather of the Southern Hemisphere and is drought tolerant once established.
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape; widely cultivated in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California, and naturalized in some regions
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower), meaning 'flower of love'.
